title: Linear Segments in Optimal-Path Shape Functions
statement: Consider lazy paths $S:\{0,\ldots,n\}\to\mathbb Z$ with $\lvert S(i+1)-S(i)\rvert\leq1$ in the product random potential $V(x,i)=F(x)b(i)$, where the fields $\{F(x)\}$ and $\{b(i)\}$ are independent and i.i.d., the potential has a compactly supported density positive on the interior of its support, and $\mathbb E[b(i)]=0$. Does the shape function for the minimum action of point-to-point paths have a nontrivial linear segment near the origin?
background:

## Literature review (checked 2026-08-21)

**Status:** partially solved

**Assessment.** For the product-type random environment, later work proves a flat linear edge near the origin under an explicit power-law condition on the density at the support edge; this establishes the conjecture in a substantial regime but not under every assumption stated in the extracted record.
